tool.name: hgt-site
tool.description: call candidate horizontal gene transfer sites from host alignments and Kraken2 calls
tool.command: #if $alignment.ext == 'sam' ln -s '$alignment' input.sam && #set $aln = 'input.sam' #else ln -s '$alignment' input.bam && #set $aln = 'input.bam' #end if hgt-site call --bam '$aln' --kraken #for $k in $kraken '$k' #end for --host-taxid $host_taxid #if $nodes --nodes '$nodes' #end if --threads \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1} --min-mapq $advanced.min_mapq --min-support $advanced.min_support --max-qvalue $advanced.max_qvalue -o '$sites' --bed '$bed' --vcf '$vcf'

param.name: alignment
param.label: Paired-end reads aligned to the host genome

param.name: kraken
param.label: Kraken2 per-read output for the unmapped reads
param.help: The per-read output of Kraken2 (not the report). Read names must match the alignment. Several files can be selected if a pipeline wrote more than one per sample.

param.name: host_taxid
param.label: NCBI taxonomy ID of the host
param.help: For example 9606 for human or 10090 for mouse.

param.name: nodes
param.label: NCBI nodes.dmp (optional)
param.help: With the NCBI taxonomy, reads classified anywhere in the host lineage are ignored, not only those assigned to the host taxid itself.

param.name: min_mapq
param.label: Minimum mapping quality of an anchor read

param.name: min_support
param.label: Minimum supporting read pairs for a site

param.name: max_qvalue
param.label: Maximum q-value of the enrichment test

tool.help:
**What it does**
hgt-site finds places where DNA from bacteria or other organisms may have been inserted into a host genome, using paired-end sequencing data. Most bacterial reads in these samples come from contamination or from DNA fragments joined by chance in the lab, so hgt-site checks each possible site against what chance alone would produce and keeps only the sites with clearly more support.
**Inputs**
- Paired-end reads aligned to the host genome (BAM or SAM). - Kraken2 per-read output for the reads that did not map to the host. Read names must match those in the alignment. - The NCBI taxonomy ID of the host.
**Outputs**
- A table with one row per candidate site: position, supporting read pairs, main foreign taxon, enrichment statistics, flags, and a filter column that says PASS or lists the reasons a site failed. - A BED file of the sites that passed every filter. - A VCF file of every candidate site, with PASS or the failing flags in the FILTER column.
**Reading the results**
Four columns decide whether a site is worth following up: ``n_pairs`` against ``expected_pairs``, which is how many pairs chance alone would have put there; ``qvalue``; ``top_taxid_fraction``, where a value near 1.0 means the support comes from one organism; and the split-read counts, where any at all is the strongest evidence in the table.
A site that passed is a lead rather than a finding. hgt-site has been validated on simulated reads from real genomes and not on real sequencing data with confirmed integrations.
**More**
Documentation: https://iraajgangavaram.github.io/hgt-site/
Benchmarks and source: https://github.com/iraajgangavaram/hgt-site
